locator: VIII.3, 254a24-25: εἶναι τὸ ὂν ἄπειρον καὶ ἀκίνητον
interpretation: Aristotle reports, without naming them, those who say that being is infinite and unmoved (Melissus' formula), and earlier (253a32-b2) calls the claim that all things are at rest, sought by setting perception aside, an infirmity of thought. Read as the thesis that nothing is being moved in any respect. The report is Aristotle's; no Eleatic text is pinned. The formalization keeps only the present-tense denial of motion, not 'infinite'.
